<task>استخرج من المصدر المحدد الأرقام الدقيقة لعدد الرجال وعدد النساء الذين أكملوا التعليم العالي في تعداد 2011. سجّل القيم بوحدة الأشخاص (أو بالحالة إذا كانت بالألوف، اذكر ذلك بدقة) ومع رابط/مرجع الصفحة كدليل داخل المعمل.</task>

<task>احسب الفرق: اطرح العدد الأصغر من العدد الأكبر (المطلوب مجرد القيمة المطلقة للفرق). ثم قدّم الفرق بصيغة "عدد آلاف النساء" حسب تعليمات السؤال (أي إذا كان هناك 30.1 ألف رجل أكثر، النتيجة تكون "30.1"). تأكد من تدوير/التقريب وفق ما يظهر في المصادر (إبقاء خانة عشرية كما في أمثلة السؤال إذا كانت متاحة).</task>
<task>تحقق من النتيجة عبر مصدر بديل أو عبر إعادة استخراج من نفس المصدر (مثلاً جدول آخر أو ملف PDF رسمي). بعد التحقق، أعِد صياغة المشكلة النهائية إلى هذا الشكل الخاص المطلوب لتنفيذ الإجابة النهائية: "خذ أعداد الرجال والنساء الذين أكملوا التعليم العالي (من تعداد بلغاريا 2011): رجال = X (ألف)، نساء = Y (ألف). اطرح الأصغر من الأكبر وأعطِ الفرق بالألوف كنص رقمي فقط (مثال: 30.1)". أرفق في هذه الصيغة تعليمًا صريحًا للمُنفذ النهائي: "أرجو إرجاع الإجابة النهائية فقط كرقم واحد بصيغة آلاف (مثال: 30.1) دون أي شرح". </task>

Lx = (d/dx * (A * x²)) + 4997 ناقص C
حيث L هو آخر رقمين من سنة إعلان استقلال فنزويلا، وA هو عدد ألوان شعار TikTok حتى يوليو 2023، باستثناء الأسود والأبيض، وC هو متوسط ​​طول المرأة في الفلبين وفقًا لمقال نُشر في موقع Business Insider في يوليو 2023، مقربًا لأقرب سنتيمتر صحيح.
english_question:
Find the value of x to the nearest tenth: Lx = (d/dx * (A * x-squared)) + 4-thousand'n'ninety-7 minus C
Where L is the last two digits of the year of the Venezuelan Declaration of Independence,
A is the number of colors in the TikTok logo as of July 2023, excluding black and white,
and C is the height of the average woman in the Philippines according to a July 2023 Business Insider article, rounded to the nearest whole centimeter
agent_plan:

<task>Search for documentation or reliable sources describing the TikTok logo's colors as of July 2023. Determine the number of distinct colors in the logo excluding black and white (this yields A). Prefer official brand resources or reputable design/tech articles.</task>
<task>Locate the Business Insider article published in July 2023 that reports the average height of women in the Philippines. Extract the reported average female height value and round it to the nearest whole centimeter to produce C. Use only the Business Insider item specified by the problem for this value.</task>
<task>Compute x from the given expression using the retrieved numeric values. Steps: note that d/dx (A * x^2) = 2A x, so the equation Lx = 2A x + 4997 - C leads to x = (4997 - C) / (L - 2A). <task>Verify the computed x by (a) cross-checking the three retrieved factual values (L, A, C) against at least one alternative reputable source each, and (b) re-evaluating the arithmetic. Then present the final required output in this exact special format (only the final number rounded to one decimal, no extra text): Provide the numeric values L, A, and C, the substitution into x = (4997 - C) / (L - 2A), and then return only the final x rounded to the nearest tenth (e.g., 12.3).</task>
</tasks>

english_question:
Here's a fun riddle that I think you'll enjoy.

You have been selected to play the final round of the hit new game show "Pick That Ping-Pong". In this round, you will be competing for a large cash prize. Your job will be to pick one of several different numbered ping-pong balls, and then the game will commence. The host describes how the game works.

A device consisting of a winding clear ramp and a series of pistons controls the outcome of the game. The ramp feeds balls onto a platform. The platform has room for three ping-pong balls at a time. The three balls on the platform are each aligned with one of three pistons. At each stage of the game, one of the three pistons will randomly fire, ejecting the ball it strikes. If the piston ejects the ball in the first position on the platform the balls in the second and third position on the platform each advance one space, and the next ball on the ramp advances to the third position. If the piston ejects the ball in the second position, the ball in the first position is released and rolls away, the ball in the third position advances two spaces to occupy the first position, and the next two balls on the ramp advance to occupy the second and third positions on the platform. If the piston ejects the ball in the third position, the ball in the first position is released and rolls away, the ball in the second position advances one space to occupy the first position, and the next two balls on the ramp advance to occupy the second and third positions on the platform.

The ramp begins with 100 numbered ping-pong balls, arranged in ascending order from 1 to 100. The host activates the machine and the first three balls, numbered 1, 2, and 3, advance to the platform. Before the random firing of the pistons begins, you are asked which of the 100 balls you would like to pick. If your pick is ejected by one of the pistons, you win the grand prize, $10,000.

Which ball should you choose to maximize your odds of winning the big prize? Please provide your answer as the number of the ball selected.
agent_plan:
<tasks>
<task>Read and formalize the game rules precisely: confirm the platform state representation (three slots indexed 1..3), the piston selection being uniform among the three pistons each round, and the deterministic update rules for platform and ramp when piston hits slot 1, 2, or 3. Produce a concise state-transition description that a solver can use (no probability computation yet).</task>
<task>Identify what the solver must compute: for each ball numbered 1..100, compute the probability that this ball is eventually ejected by a piston at the moment it is hit while occupying whatever platform slot (i.e., the probability that the ball triggers the grand prize). Clarify the start conditions (initial platform contains balls 1,2,3; ramp supplies balls 4..100 in order), termination conditions (process continues until ramp empties and platform operations finish), and that piston choice each round is uniform and independent. Return this computational specification in a precise form the reasoning/coding agent can directly use.</task>
<task>Delegate the full reasoning/calculation task (analytical computation or Monte Carlo simulation) to a capable solver: ask them to compute the win-probability for every ball 1..100 under the specified process, find which ball maximizes that probability, and output only that ball number. Require that if they use simulation they run enough trials to estimate probabilities with high confidence (reporting is allowed internally, but final output must be just the single integer). Note: because this is a pure-probability reasoning/computation problem that does not require external facts, instruct the solver to perform the entire computation (analytical or coded) themselves and return the single-number answer.</task>
<task>Transform the original problem into a compact formal input for the solver (so they can run code or do exact reasoning). Provide the model, initial state, transition function, random choice distribution, objective, and required final output format. Concretely present:
- Balls: sequence 1..100 (ramp order).
- Platform: slots S1,S2,S3 initially = [1,2,3] (S1 is position closest to piston 1).
- Each round: choose i uniformly from {1,2,3}. If i=1: remove S1 (it is ejected), S2->S1, S3->S2, next ramp ball -> S3 (if any remain). If i=2: remove S2 (ejected), S3->S1, next ramp ball -> S2 (if any), next ramp ball -> S3 (if any). If i=3: remove S3 (ejected), S2->S1, next ramp ball -> S2 (if any), next ramp ball -> S3 (if any). Continue until no balls remain on ramp and platform (process ends when there are no balls left to fill slots and eventually all are ejected). Objective: for each ball n in 1..100 compute P_n = probability ball n is ejected (i.e., is the removal target at the time it is removed). Output requirement: return only the single integer n* that maximizes P_n. Provide this as the exact input specification to start the computation.</task>
</tasks>

I've got a Boggle board here:

ABRL
EITE
IONS
FPEI

I'd like to know the longest word that can be generated from the board. Please find the longest English language word that can be generated from this board. If more than one word of the same length exists at the maximum word length, please report the longest word that comes first, alphabetically. <task>Download the specified dictionary file "mawu_alpha" (the english-words word list) from the given GitHub repository (https://github.com/dwyl/english-words). Retrieve the raw word list file (words_alpha.txt or the equivalent raw URL) and save a local copy for processing.</task>
<task>Preprocess the downloaded word list: load it into memory, normalize to lowercase, strip whitespace, and optionally remove any non-alphabetic entries. Also produce a filtered set of candidate words whose lengths are at least 3 (typical Boggle minimum) and whose letters are all present in the board’s multiset (quick prefilter to reduce search space).</task>
<task>Implement a Boggle solver in code (Python recommended). The solver must:
- Represent the board as a 4x4 grid with rows "ABRL", "EITE", "IONS", "FPEI".
- Use standard Boggle adjacency (8 neighbors) and disallow reusing the same cell in a single word.
- For each candidate dictionary word, efficiently check whether it can be formed using DFS/backtracking on the board.
- Collect all valid English words from the dictionary that are found on the board.</task>
<task>Execute the solver with the preprocessed dictionary to find all valid words on the board. From the results, identify the maximum word length found, then produce the subset of words that have that maximum length. If multiple words share that maximum length, sort them alphabetically and keep the ones that come first (i.e., return the full sorted list of all maximum-length words, so the caller can pick according to the tie rule).</task>
<task>Verify the results by re-running the solver or using an alternative verification method (for example, cross-checking a random sample of found long words by performing a targeted DFS search per word or running the solver with a second pass of stricter filtering). Report any discrepancies and reconcile to ensure final list is correct.</task>
<task>Produce the final output in the requested format: return only the final list (array) of the longest English words found on the board, in alphabetical order if multiple tie. To enable the final agent to produce the answer, here is the explicit problem specification for execution:
- Board (4x4 rows): ["ABRL", "EITE", "IONS", "FPEI"]
- Dictionary file: local path to the downloaded words_alpha.txt (from https://github.com/dwyl/english-words)
- Boggle rules: 8-direction adjacency, no cell reused in a word, minimum word length 3
- Output: list of the longest valid English words found on the board (if multiple, return all tied longest words sorted alphabetically)
Please write and run Python code that performs the above and return only the final list of words as the answer.</task>
</tasks>

Rather than using alternate weights of 1 and 3, the checksum digit is calculated with an alternate weight of 1 and some other positive integer less than 10. These errored columns do not involve the final column or one of the first three columns. Using this information, please provide all potential solutions with the unknown weight and the smaller index of the two errored columns (assume we start our indexing at 0 and ignore hyphens). Give your answer in the form x, y where x is the weight and y is the smaller index of the two transposed columns.

978-946669746-1
978-398036139-6
978-447656680-4

Produce a precise spec (inputs, outputs, and success condition) that will be used as the implementation contract.</task>

<task>Task 3 — Implement and run the search (delegate as one unit): Using the parsed list of ten 13-digit numbers (hyphens removed) and the specs from Task 2, write and execute code that tries all integer weights w from 2 through 9 and all swap indices i from 3 through 10. Return all pairs (w,i) for which every entry becomes valid after performing the described swap. Provide the complete code used and the raw results. (Note: do not break this step into smaller reasoning steps; produce and run the code as one unit and report results.)</task>

<task>Task 4 — Verify and cross-check results: Independently re-run the check using a second method (for example, a small alternative implementation or manual spot-checks on a few entries) to confirm the pairs found in Task 3 are correct. Neno la tufaha limechukuliwa kutoka Kiingereza katika Tizin, na kwa hivyo ni "Apple" ni umbo la nomino, "Zapple" ni umbo la accusative, na "Izapple" ni umbo la genitive. When it is used in the present, it is used in it's root form, when it is used in the preterit past, it is "Tay", and when it is used in the imperfect past, it is "Aktay". It is used differently than in English, and is better translated as "is pleasing to", meaning that the thing doing the liking is actually the object of the sentence rather than the subject.

The word for apples is borrowed from English in Tizin, and so it is "Apple" is the nominative form, "Zapple" is the accusative form, and "Izapple" is the genitive form.

Also note the lexical facts about "apple": Apple = noun form (Pa), Zapple = accusative (Mato), Izapple = genitive (Sing).</task>
<task>Determine the mapping of the source sentence "Ninapenda maapulo" into roles under the Tizin semantics: identify the semantic agent, patient, and which entity corresponds to the thing that “pleases” (i.e., which must be the subject in Tizin). Decide which noun-case forms (Pa/Mato/Sing) should be used for each entity in the Tizin sentence given the grammar and the verb semantics.</task>
<task>Assemble the Tizin sentence structure using the extracted rules: choose the correct verb form (Maktay for present), place the verb first, then the direct object in its appropriate case, then the subject in its appropriate case; ensure the apple lexeme uses the correct Tizin form (Apple/Zapple/Izapple) per the case decisions made in the previous subtask. Ensure the final output follows the constraint: return only the final string in the requested format.</task>
<task>Transform the original problem into a final, explicit instruction for the agent who will produce the translation. Include all necessary rules and constraints so the agent can produce the final Tizin string directly. For example: "Translate the Swahili sentence 'Ninapenda maapulo' into Tizin. Use verb-first word order (Verb DirectObject Subject). Use the verb root 'Maktay' for present tense. Note that the verb means 'to please' (so the thing that is liked is the grammatical subject in Tizin). Noun-case forms: general noun = Pa, accusative = Mato, genitive = Sing.
